{{Quote|The A-wing is the fastest fighter we have, capable of matching a TIE Interceptor in speed.|[[General/Legends|General]] [[Carlist Rieekan/Legends|Carlist Rieekan]]|<ref name="RS I">[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron (video game)|''Star Wars: Rogue Squadron'']]</ref>}}
The '''RZ-1 A-wing interceptor''' was a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] designed by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. One of the fastest mass-produced [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptors]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the known galaxy]], the A-wing was even faster than the Imperials' [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptor]], despite also having shielding and a hyperdrive, unlike the cheaper TIE model.

==Characteristics==
[[File:Awing_egvv.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A-wing [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]
The RZ-1 A-wing [[Interceptor/Legends|interceptor]] was a small, wedge-shaped craft with a central [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] attached to twin engines. Like its [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] predecessor, the [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2]], the A-wing required [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]] of exceptional skill to take full advantage of the vessel's speed, agility, and special features.

The A-wing's [[Novaldex/Legends|Novaldex]] [[J-77 "Event Horizon" sublight engine/Legends|J-77]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]]<ref name="DB">''[[StarWars.com]] [[Databank (original)|Databank]]''</ref> remained some of the most powerful sublight thrusters two decades after the A-wing's creation. However, the highly sensitive controls made the craft exceptionally difficult to handle. Pilots had to adjust the two dorsal and two ventral stabilizer wings with great care, as even a minor turn could send the A-wing into a massive spinout.

The A-wing's wing-mounted laser cannons could rotate up and down sixty degrees for greater fire control thanks to a short [[hydro-servo bearing]] at the end of each wing tip. Some of A-wings even had their guns modified to swivel in a complete 360-degree arc, providing a surprise to any chasing fighter. However, the cannon mounts had a high rate of mechanical failure, and contributed to the fighter's extremely costly maintenance-to-flight ratio. This, among other reasons, contributed to the difficulty of keeping a squadron of A-wings operational for any length of time.<ref name="CCS" /><ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref>

The combination of sensitive controls, unmatched sublight thrust, maneuverable weapon systems, advanced sensory and stealth packages, and fragility, strained even the best pilots. In addition, the A-wing had no [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] to manage its weapons systems, requiring pilots to split their attention between flying the craft, & operating the weapon systems.

The craft had an access panel on the forward bow, and carried two [[Dymek/Legends|Dymek]] [[HM-6 Concussion Missile Launcher/Legends|HM-6 Concussion Missile Launchers]] along the sides. Each launcher was capable of launching 6 concussion missiles.<ref name="CCS" /> Thrust control jets were at the rear of the craft, just behind the rear [[Sirplex/Legends|Sirplex]] [[Z-9 deflector shield projector/Legends|Z-9 deflector shield projector]]. The engines, capable of propelling the starfighter to up to 1300 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]] per [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]] and 120 [[Megalight|MGLT]], were placed in the aft of the craft and had thrust vector controls. The A-wing carried a sensor [[Jammer/Legends|jamming unit]],<ref name="RS I guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> including a [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] [[ANs-7e sensor unit]] with [[PA-94 long-range phased tachyon detection array/Legends|PA-94 long range phased tachyon detection array]] and [[PG-7u short-range primary threat analysis grid/Legends|PG-7u short range primary threat analysis grid]], along with targeting systems in the form of a [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] [[ANq 3.6 sensor computer/Legends|ANq 3.6 tracking computer]] and an [[IN-344-B "Sightline" holographic imaging system/Legends|IN-344-B "Sightline" imaging system]]<ref name="SC" /> The avionics were a [[Torplex/Legends|Torplex]] [[Rq9.Z advanced flight control avionics package|Rq9.z flight control]] system.<ref name="SC" /> The craft carried one [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] and up to 40 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] of cargo.<ref name="RS I guide" />

<div style="float:right">[[File:ProtonRocket--XWMRebAces.png|thumb|200px|An A-wing firing a [[Proton rocket/Legends|proton rocket]]]]</div>
The weapons carried on-board, including [[advanced concussion missile]]s, gave the craft the power to engage large targets<ref name="RS III guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> up to and including [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Imperial Star Destroyers]].<ref name="RS I guide" />

Many of the starfighters were produced in underground factories, and at least one at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] had [[fijisi]] wood panels.<ref name="Bacta War" /> The A-wings were maintenance-heavy and prone to breakdowns, although the sensor jammers and concussion weapons were effective in lightning raids.<ref name="EGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>

Although a capable starfighter, the a-wing was especially notable for its intelligence-gathering and reconnaissance missions, in large part because of its hyperdrive capability, speed, and maneuverability. The ship was littered with concealed multi-spectral imagers and other sensors, which allowed it to gather information about an enemy. These abilities were further enhanced by its sensor-jamming system, which was powerful enough to disrupt detection and targeting systems of TIE fighters and other small vessels, although they were ineffective against capital ships, and acted as a double-edged sword due to the jamming system giving a precise lock on the fighter if detected by the enemy. As such, experienced pilots learned to drop out of hyperspace close to an enemy fleet or space-installation, make a blistering run around (or even through) the enemy formation, using the A-wing's on-board imagers and sensors to gather information, and then escape to hyperspace before being detected.<ref name="CCS" />

The A-wing's wedge-shaped prow was fitted with a reinforced heat shield. Although this was intended to protect the craft during atmospheric entry, it also acted as a makeshift battering ram. However, this ramming maneuver was largely used by pilots as a last resort, with the pilots relying on the nose wedge to breach an enemy ship's hull and either cripple or outright destroy it.<ref name="CCS" /> This tactic was famously demonstrated by [[Arvel Crynyd/Legends|Arvel Crynyd]] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], where he rammed the bridge of the Star Dreadnought ''Executor''.<ref name="SWE6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

==History==
===Development===
[[File:CCS_A-wing.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A-wing cross-section.]]
[[General/Legends|General]] [[Jan Dodonna/Legends|Jan Dodonna's]] after action review of the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] affirmed the value of Alliance starfighters, but also highlighted that a simple trio of [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] starfighters had almost foiled the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|trench run]]. Dodonna planned to create a dedicated Alliance interceptor, in anticipation of a similar analysis by the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]]; indeed, [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]] accelerated work on an updated [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE Interceptor]] which would match the A-wing's speed.

To design the starfighter, Dodonna turned to [[Walex Blissex/Legends|Walex Blissex]], famed ex-[[Kuat Systems Engineering/Legends|Kuat Systems Engineering]] engineer. Blissex brought valuable experience from work on the Clone Wars-era [[Delta-7 Aethersprite-class light interceptor/Legends|Delta-7 ''Aetherspite''-class light interceptor]] and [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|Alpha-3]] interceptors. The pair based initial designs on the [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearhead]], already nicknamed by pilots as "A-wings" per the ''-wing'' naming convention for other Rebel craft, of which two had fought at Yavin. They formed [[Alliance Underground Engineering]],<ref name="DB" /> and worked with pilot [[Jake Farrell/Legends|Jake Farrell]]<ref name="EGW" /> in improving a [[Tammuz-an/Legends|Tammuz-an]] design.<ref name="DB" /> It was additionally based off the Delta-7.<ref name="AOR CB" />

===Early production===
[[File:Awing-NEGVV.png|thumb|180px|An A-wing, view on its engines.]]
The reduced budget forced Dodonna and Blissex to substantially modify the original design. Blissex redrafted to use components readily available from [[Ordnance and Supply/Legends|Ordnance and Supply Command]], pushing each beyond factory specifications.

The earliest A-wings were hand-assembled at Alliance facilities like [[Cardooine/Legends|Cardooine]] and [[Chardaan Shipyards]]. This resulted in interesting modifications; some fighters incorporated actual wood furnishings for the cockpit interior, such as the one that Rogue Squadron pilot Tycho Celchu flew during the Battle of Endor.<ref name="Bacta War" /> In [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]], the [[Soaring Dactillions]] were assigned the prototypes to fly at the Cardooine [[Rebel base (Cardooine)|Rebel base]]. After a [[Standard week/Legends|week]], they came under [[Assault on Cardooine|attack]] by the Empire, and the Dactillions flew the fighter in battle. Although they proved that the starfighter had superb qualities, only two of the pilots survived.<ref name="Zal">[[Takeover at Whisper Base (adventure)|''Takeover at Whisper Base (Adventure Book)'']] Zal Ace Character Folio</ref>

More serious was the slow production rate, allowing the fielding of just a few full squadrons. Only one full unit, [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Green Squadron]], was present at the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]] in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]]. Elsewhere, A-wings were issued to a handful of crack units, like [[Nomad Squadron]] and [[Pash Cracken/Legends|Pash Cracken's]] wing.

===Operational deployment===
{{Quote|Any pilot who volunteers to fly an A-wing better be brave or crazy. Probably helps to be a little of both.|General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="NEGVV" />}}
The Rebel Alliance acquired some A-wings at some point after the Battle of Yavin, which they eventually used for the first time when [[Ison Corridor ambush|ambushed]] by Imperial forces in the [[Ison Trade Corridor/Legends|Ison Corridor]].<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>

[[File:ObjectsInViewportAreCloserThanTheyAppear-ROTJ.png|thumb|left|250px|Arvel Crynyd steers his A-wing into the bridge of ''Executor'' during the Battle of Endor.]]
The Rebel's [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] employed A-wings during the [[Search for the Nonnah|search]] for the starship ''[[Nonnah]]''<ref name="RS I guide" /> around six months after the Battle of Yavin.<ref name="RS I guide" /> The squadron also employed it during a [[Battle above Taloraan|battle above]] Taloraan.<ref name="RS I" /> [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] flew it during a [[Raid on Bespin|raid]] on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]],<ref name="RS II" /> and also flew the starfighter during a [[Mission to Destrillion|strike]] at [[Destrillion]].<ref name="RS III">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref> Rebel pilot [[Ace Azzameen/Legends|Ace Azzameen]] also flew the A-wing during a number of missions with the [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance Fleet]].<ref name="XWA" /> A lone A-wing piloted by [[Arvel Crynyd/Legends|Arvel Crynyd]] played a major role when it helped to destroy the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Star Dreadnought]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']] during the Battle of Endor, by ramming its bridge, causing the entire ship to fall and crash into the second Death Star.<ref name="SWE6" />

The A-wing was also used by the Alliance's successor as galactic government: the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="DFR" /> In [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], Rogue Squadron pilot [[Tycho Celchu/Legends|Tycho Celchu]] led [[Surprise Squadron]] at the [[Taking of Kuat|capture]] of [[Kuat/Legends|Kuat]]. Their A-wings were equipped with experimental ion torpedoes. The mission was a success and the massive [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyards]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] Kuat fell into New Republic hands.<ref name="EGW" />

A-wings also participated in the [[Battle of Calamari|attack]] on [[Dac/Legends|Mon Calamari]], where several were destroyed by [[World Devastator]]s.<ref name="RS I" />

In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], A-wings were stationed on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Gold-striped craft escorted [[Kir Kanos]]' shuttle to a landing pad when it entered restricted airspace near the [[Imperial Palace/Legends|Royal Palace]]. A-wings were also assigned to General [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo's]] fleet for [[Battle of Pallaxides|mop-up operations]] around that time. A contingent of A-wings was also carried on-board a Mon Calamari Star Cruiser captained by [[Lar Ndigo]], who was assigned to Solo's fleet and was detached to reconnoiter the planetoid [[RZ7-6113-23]]. The A-wings fought off attacking [[Restored Empire]] [[Alpha-3 Nimbus-class V-wing starfighter/Legends|V-Wing starfighters]] during the ensuring [[Battle of RZ7-6113-23|battle]] over the planetoid.<ref name="CE III">''[[Star Wars: Crimson Empire III: Empire Lost]]''</ref>

Later, after the peace treaty with the Galactic Empire, A-wings were flown by pilots of [[Kyp's Dozen]] to hunt [[Smuggler/Legends|smugglers]] before the squadron was decimated by [[Yuuzhan Vong]] pilots.<ref name="VP">''[[The New Jedi Order: Vector Prime]]''</ref>

In [[44 ABY]], two A-wings were assigned to the [[Galactic Alliance Starfighter Command]] contingent at [[Skifter Station]] [[Orbit/Legends|orbiting]] [[Kuratooine]].<ref name="X:MK" />

[[File:AwingSpaceBattle-SWI40.jpg|thumb|right|180px|An A-wing in battle]]
Though it had been designed to defend immobile stations or slow-moving Alliance starships from starfighter raids, the A-wing was pressed into service as a quick-strike fighter as part of the post-Yavin Alliance strategy of guerrilla warfare. Using its impressive straight-line acceleration and advanced jamming package, A-wings were able to hit targets before they could respond, and then flee before any defense could be organized.

This change found its apex in a devastating tactic known as the [[A-wing Slash/Legends|A-wing Slash]] which was developed by [[General/Legends|General]] [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]]. A group of [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wings]] would approach an Imperial convoy, hiding a number of A-wings in their drive exhaust. The X-wings would then pull away, diverting attention away from the speedy A-wings, which could launch HM-6 [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missiles]] against the convoy and pull away.

[[File:A-wing2.jpg|thumb|left|180px|An A-wing in action.]]
The A-wing also found use in reconnaissance missions, and would become a favorite among Fleet Intelligence and [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] operatives for its speed. A team of A-wings could exit [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] near an Imperial objective, begin jamming enemy sensors, draw scans and [[Hologram/Legends|holographic]] imagery, and retreat before being detected. If it was detected, the pilots could easily outrun any pursuers, ensuring the safety of the pilots and the intelligence.

While the A-wing became popular for "hit-and-fade" raids and reconnaissance duty, it was required to operate from a nearby base of operations or carrier ship because of its navigational computer's limitations, which could only store coordinates for two hyperspace jumps before requiring calibration.

The TIE/IN interceptor, better known as the TIE Interceptor, was perhaps the Empire's closest equivalent to the A-wing. The Interceptor had two more laser cannons and better agility which gave it an edge in a dogfight, but its lack of shields and warhead launchers limited its durability and tactical usage. The Interceptor was (like all mass-produced TIEs) generally available in larger numbers, but A-wing pilots tended to be more skilled as they had a higher survival rate than their Interceptor counterparts. In a pure chase, the A-wing could outrun the Interceptor, however this was only if the A-wing was undamaged. Later Imperial starfighters such as the [[TIE/ad starfighter|TIE Avenger]], [[TIE/d "Defender" Multi-Role Starfighter/Legends|TIE Defender]], and [[Missile Boat]] were easily more than a match for the A-wing, however they were never mass-produced due to turmoil in the Imperial Navy.

===Replacement===
[[File:Awings_dfr.jpg|thumb|right|180px|A-wings in a skirmish during the [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]] campaign.]]
Shortly after the Battle of Endor, the [[Mark II A-wing]] entered production. While A-wings were originally built on an individual basis by the Alliance itself, the Mark II was mass produced by the [[Incom Corporation/Legends|Incom Corporation]]. One notable alteration was that the laser cannons of the A-wing Mark II were configured for full 360-degree rotation.

The value of a high speed interceptor was clear, but the A-wing had major defensive and navigational limitations. Thus, new starfighters like the [[E-7 E-wing multi-role starfighter|E-wing]] or T-65AC4 X-wing were created with comparable speed, but some models were given heavier shields and armor, [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] compatibility, and more powerful weapons. Despite the introduction of newer starfighters and efforts to standardize fleet operations, the A-wing's exceptional design allowed it to endure through the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]].

==Behind the scenes==
Production paintings for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] show the A-wing painted in blue markings, but these were changed to red to allow the models to be filmed for bluescreen. According to the [[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''X-wing'']] games, red signifies [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]]. A-wings from other squadrons bear their respective color. One Star Wars Action Fleet A-wing model has green markings instead of red, supporting this claim.

[[File:MCQ-awing.jpg|thumb|left|200px|A-wing concept art by [[Ralph McQuarrie]].]]
The craft was originally known only as "A fighter" during the production of ''Return of the Jedi''.

A-wings appear in the games ''[[Star Wars: Empire at War]]'', ''Star Wars: X-wing'', ''[[Star Wars: Rebel Assault]]'' and the [[Star Wars: Droids: The Adventures of R2-D2 and C-3PO|''Droids'']] animated series; however, these are set years before the A-wing is stated to have been developed, making it an anomaly. All these pre-Yavin A-wing instances have been [[Retroactive continuity|retconned]] into [[R-22 Spearhead starfighter|R-22 Spearheads]].

Like other ships ([[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']], for example), the size of the A-wing is in dispute. Fans argue that the 9.6 meters and the derived width and height are too big, because visual evidence from ''Return of the Jedi'' seems to suggest the A-wing is very small compared to other starfighters; close-up shots of A-wing pilots show that the cockpit is cramped, and suggest the entire ship cannot be very large.

A size analysis of the studio model used for ''Return of the Jedi'' suggests that the length of the ship is half as long as the documented 9.6 meters. [[Star Wars Technical Journal of the Rebel Forces]] states the model is 60 cm long and the pilot figure a 1/8 scale action figure, which results into a length of 4.8 meters. However, it should be noted that it is entirely possible the 1/8 figure was only used because it fit in the cockpit of the model.

Another way to determine the size by comparing the headroom of the pilot with the relative size of the cockpit to the entire fighter, would be to compare the cockpit film set with the studio model.

The size comparison chart found in the 2011 reference book ''[[Millennium Falcon Owner's Workshop Manual]]'' also depicts an RZ-1 A-wing. By using the well documented sizes of the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] and the [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] as a scale, the resulting A-wing size is roughly 7.0 meters.

Although it is unknown on what the original 9.6 meter figure is based on, like the issue on [[Home One/Legends|''Home One'']], the official length remains 9.6 meters until a canon source states otherwise.

The weapons payload of the A-wing varies from source to source, with some not having the concussion missile launchers, and some saying that the laser cannons are actually blaster cannons. In ''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]'' for example, A-wings are armed with repeating laser cannons and homing cluster missiles.

[[The LEGO Group]] made several sets of the A-wing. The first was 7134 "A-Wing Fighter" from [[2000]]. The second is 6207 "A-Wing Fighter" from [[2006]]. Both A-wings have [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red Squadron]] markings. Finally, the third set to have an A-wing was 7754 "Home One Mon Calamari Star Cruiser" from [[August]] [[2009]]. Unlike the previous A-wings, this one sported [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Green Squadron]] markings. In January of [[2013]] a fourth A-Wing was released, the [http://lego.wikia.com/wiki/75003_A-Wing_Starfighter 75003 A-Wing] with a pilot with a more realistic helmet.
